comment: Doctrine TEMPLATES for permanent/standing work that lives outside the sprint structure (trading desks, bug-bounty lanes, on-call watches). A team ADOPTS one of these (POST /api/team-doctrine/<teamId>/adopt), which copies the levels onto the team's own record as their live doctrine; the team then OWNS its copy and modifies it freely (PUT /api/team-doctrine/<teamId>) without touching this file or any other team. Adopting again resets the copy back to the template. Level ids are strings; names are whatever the team calls them (DEFCON, green/amber/red, anything). The tank stores levels and routes notify pings; it never interprets trigger/staffing/autonomy/demote -- those are the team's own words, surfaced in team status and Telegram.

bug-bounty.name: Bug bounty desk
bug-bounty.description: Vulnerability research with hard safety rails. Escalation is driven by the blast radius of what was found and how close work is to touching a live target.

levels.name: DEFCON 5 - routine recon
levels.trigger: normal hunting day; nothing found or trivial low-severity findings
levels.autonomy: read-only recon on in-scope targets; draft reports internally

levels.name: DEFCON 4 - active lead
levels.trigger: a plausible finding needs reproduction work
levels.autonomy: reproduction against OWN lab replicas only; no third-party systems

levels.name: DEFCON 3 - confirmed finding
levels.trigger: reproducible finding of medium severity confirmed in the lab
levels.autonomy: write the report, prepare disclosure, NO contact with the vendor yet

levels.name: DEFCON 2 - disclosure window
levels.autonomy: correspond with the vendor per the disclosure policy; nothing else external

levels.name: DEFCON 1 - actively exploited
levels.trigger: evidence the finding is being exploited in the wild
levels.autonomy: nothing autonomous beyond reading; every external action needs the operator

trading-desk.name: Trading desk
trading-desk.description: Capital risk states. Escalation is driven by drawdown and volatility, never by profit (a good day is still DEFCON 5).

levels.name: STEADY - normal ops
levels.trigger: drawdown under 2% and volatility within the model's expected band
levels.autonomy: paper trades and analysis freely; live orders only inside the pre-approved playbook

levels.name: ELEVATED - watch
levels.trigger: drawdown 2-5% or volatility above the 80th percentile
levels.autonomy: reduce position sizes; no new strategies; log every order with a reason
levels.demote: two calm sessions in a row

levels.name: CAUTION - defensive
levels.autonomy: close or hedge into the defensive book; no new entries

levels.name: HIGH - capital freeze
levels.autonomy: flatten risk only; every action reported, none initiated without the operator

levels.name: CRITICAL - full stop
levels.trigger: drawdown over 15%, or funds moved unexpectedly
levels.autonomy: read-only. Report. Nothing moves without the operator.

on-call.name: On-call watch
on-call.description: Keeping services and monitors healthy. Escalation follows alert severity and how much of the tank's own work is impacted.

levels.name: AMBER - degraded
levels.autonomy: diagnose and fix inside the affected service

levels.name: ORANGE - user impact
levels.trigger: agents or the player are visibly blocked
levels.staffing: watcher + senior on the affected surface
levels.autonomy: restarts, rollbacks, and mitigations allowed; log each one

levels.name: RED - tank down
levels.trigger: the tank itself is unreachable or a data-loss risk exists
levels.autonomy: restore service; no schema or destructive changes

levels.name: BLACK - data loss
levels.trigger: evidence of actual data loss or breach
levels.autonomy: preserve evidence, restore from backup, change nothing else
